prompt: Bounded shrubdepth implies bounded clique-width. Which class witnesses that the converse fails?

answers.explanation: Paths have clique-width at most three, but no fixed tree-model height and fixed colour count can represent paths of every length.
Cliques have height-one, one-colour tree-models, so their shrubdepth is bounded.
Use height one, one colour, and an empty adjacency signature.
Two colours on a height-one tree distinguish the sides; the signature joins exactly different colours.
Stars are complete bipartite graphs with one side of size one, so height one and two colours suffice.

answers.text: All disjoint unions of edges and isolated vertices.
answers.explanation: A height-two model groups the two endpoints of each edge; one colour and adjacency only within a group suffice.
A height-two model groups vertices by clique; use one colour and join exactly leaves in the same group.
A height-two model groups matched pairs; its signature joins leaves from different groups.
Use height-two groups for components and two colours for centres and leaves; join unlike colours only inside a group.
A height-two, one-colour model groups each independent part and joins leaves exactly across different groups.

sources.title: Ganian et al. — Shrub-depth: Capturing Height of Dense Graphs, §§2–4
